Metadata.title: CyberArena — Learn cybersecurity by practicing
Metadata.description: Personal TryHackMe-style cybersecurity learning platform: novice-to-expert paths, flag rooms, isolated Docker labs and a gamified progress system.

hero.title: Your personal cybersecurity arena
hero.subtitle: Learning paths with guided rooms, flag challenges, isolated Docker labs and a progress system with XP, levels and streaks. From Cyber Security 101 to Red Teaming.
hero.disclaimer: Educational content only, to practice in controlled local environments.

roadmap.title: Learning roadmap
roadmap.subtitle: Five paths, novice to expert, in the recommended order.

paths.title: Cyber Security 101
paths.description: Fundamentals: Linux, Windows & AD, networking, cryptography, basic exploitation, web hacking and defense.

paths.title: Jr Penetration Tester
paths.description: Reconnaissance, Nmap, Burp Suite, Metasploit, privilege escalation, OWASP and Active Directory.

paths.title: Web Application Pentesting
paths.description: OWASP in depth, APIs, injections and chained web exploitation.

paths.title: Web Application Red Teaming
paths.description: Evasion, advanced payloads and offensive engagements against web applications.

paths.title: Red Teaming
paths.description: Advanced AD, Kerberos, containers, cloud/IAM and AI/LLM exploitation (PT2 level).

tips: Don't reuse passwords: a password manager is your best ally.
Turn on two-factor authentication (2FA) wherever you can.
Before attacking, enumerate: reconnaissance decides everything else.
Read command output in full: details hide the flags.
On Linux, man <command> is the manual you always have at hand.
The principle of least privilege limits the impact of any intrusion.
A backup you have never restored is not a backup.
HTTPS encrypts the transport; it doesn't fix a vulnerable app.
Always validate on the server: the user controls the client.
Parameterized queries put an end to SQL injection.
Take notes while you practice: your future self will thank you.
Logs tell stories. Learn to read them.
Every open port is a door: ask what's behind it.
Keep software up to date: many breaches use already-patched bugs.
Hashing isn't encryption: hashes aren't decrypted, they're cracked.
Only practice in authorized environments, like the CyberArena labs.
Be wary of messages that push urgency: it's phishing's favorite trick.
Three correct answers a day keep your streak alive.
Flags usually look like FLAG{...}: copy them in full.
If you get stuck, switch rooms and come back with a fresh mind.

home: Starting from scratch? Cyber Security 101 is your first stop.
Every path goes from easy to hard. Follow the order and you won't get lost.
paths: Paths are ordered from beginner to expert. Start with the first one.
Every completed path earns you a downloadable certificate.
path: Use "Continue" to resume your first pending room.
Rooms tagged lab include a Docker environment to practice in.
room: Read the whole task before answering: clues are usually in the text.
Use the ← and → keys to move between tasks.
If you miss several times, open the hint: it doesn't cost XP.
hacktivities: Sort by "Recommended" to see rooms in path order.
Turn on "Labs only" if you feel like something hands-on.
leaderboard: The monthly ranking resets every month: there's always a chance to climb.
Every completed room adds an extra XP bonus.
dashboard: Your streak counts when you get at least three answers right per day.
From here you can continue right where you left off.
login: With an account I keep your progress, XP and certificates.
You can enable two-factor authentication from your dashboard.
status: If the API or the database fail, check docs/runbook.md.
certificate: You can download your certificate as PDF or print it.
